title: Working the Charge Due on a Cancelled Event
content:
The charge for a cancelled Private Event & Banquet Services event is the contracted event value standing in the cancellation entry for that booking, taken at the thirty-to-seven-days cancellation percentage printed against the package, and rounded to two decimal places at the end only.

## The two quantities

The contracted event value is the one the cancellation entry for that booking carries in the agreement's event ledger. The percentage is the thirty-to-seven-days cancellation percentage printed against the package the agreement is written against.

## Worked figure on hypothetical records

A cancelled booking sits on the Seated Banquet Package, whose thirty-to-seven-days percentage is 60 per cent. The cancellation entry for that booking carries a contracted event value of 11930.00.

| Quantity | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| Contracted event value in the cancellation entry | 11930.00 |
| Thirty-to-seven-days percentage printed against the package | 60 per cent |
| Charge, rounded at the end only | 7158.00 |

Were the contracted event value 11930.37, the charge would be 7158.222 before rounding and 7158.22 after it; the rounding is taken once, on the figure the percentage produces.

## Point of judgement

The value taken is the one recorded in the cancellation entry, which is the value that stood at the day written notice was given, and not any later estimate of what the event would have been worth.
